metadata.goal: Using the supplied records for one driver, investigate the driver’s operating strategy.
metadata.category: Single-driver operating strategy, cruising, order acquisition, and speed
metadata.dataset_description: A Porto Taxi case for one driver over a single ten-hour operating day. Activity segments record operating state, duration, region and linked order; the order table records request source; linked GPS points record segment trajectories and speed.

insight_list.insight: The driver spends most observed operating time cruising around the city and spends very little time waiting at a taxi stand.

plot.title: Operating-Time Allocation and Timeline
plot.description: Cruising duration and the state timeline show that taxi-stand waiting occupies only a small part of the observed day.

insight_list.question: How does the driver allocate observed operating time among cruising, taxi-stand waiting, pickup approach, and passenger service?

insight_list.insight: Most of this driver's completed orders are street hails encountered while cruising through the city.

plot.title: Street Hails within the Cruising Footprint
plot.description: Order-source composition is paired with pickup locations over the driver’s cruising trajectories.

insight_list.question: Which request sources account for this driver’s completed orders, and where do the primary-source pickups occur relative to the cruising footprint?

insight_list.insight: From 16:00 to 18:00, the driver repeatedly cruises in the central district, completes a trip after each order, then returns to the centre to cruise until the next order; most orders in this interval are street hails. Cruising locations are less fixed at other times.

plot.title: 16:00–18:00 Central Cruising Cycles
plot.description: State-coloured trajectories show central cruising, street-hail service, and subsequent returns to the centre in chronological sequence.

insight_list.question: What repeated spatial and operational sequence does the driver follow from 16:00 to 18:00, and how does it differ from cruising at other times?

insight_list.insight: The driver's cruising speed is lower than the speed while driving to a pickup or carrying a passenger.

plot.title: Speed Distributions by Operating State
plot.description: GPS-point speed distributions are compared for cruising, driving to pickup, and passenger service.

insight_list.question: How does the driver’s speed while cruising compare with speed during pickup approach and passenger service?

insights: The driver spends most observed operating time cruising around the city and spends very little time waiting at a taxi stand.
Most of this driver's completed orders are street hails encountered while cruising through the city.

From 16:00 to 18:00, the driver repeatedly cruises in the central district, completes a trip after each order, then returns to the centre to cruise until the next order; most orders in this interval are street hails. Cruising locations are less fixed at other times.
The driver's cruising speed is lower than the speed while driving to a pickup or carrying a passenger.
summary: This driver mainly operates by cruising rather than waiting at taxi stands, and most completed orders are street hails. The 16:00–18:00 period is organized around repeated central-district cruising and return cycles after street-hail trips, while other cruising is spatially less fixed. Cruising is also the driver’s slowest active driving state.
